newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Inds plans $53 mln expansion.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Inds plans $53 mln expansion.

text.p: Burlington Industries Inc said Monday it would spend $53 million to expand its Burlington Klopman Fabrics and Burlington Madison Yarn divisions to keep pace with growing product demand, resulting in approximately 190 new jobs.
The investment consists primarily of new, latest-technology equipment to be installed in five facilities in North Carolina, Virginia and Tennessee, it said.

The company said it will invest $40 million in the 1997-1999 fiscal years to increase production capacity by about 20 percent at the Burlington Klopman Fabrics division, which produces value-added synthetic fabrics for multiple end uses. All four Klopman Fabrics plants in Hurt, Virginia, Johnson City, Tennessee and Cordova and Forest City in North Carolina will be included and approximately 135 new jobs will be added in the division.

Burlington Industries said it will invest approximately $13 million over the next 14 months to expand and modernize textured yarn production at the Burlington Madison Yarn division, which manufactures both textured and spun synthetic yarns.

George Henderson, President and CEO of Burlington Industries, said, "We are excited about the opportunities for growth in our apparel fabrics business, both in the United States and around the world, which have been broadened by positive trends in global trading patterns and enhanced by NAFTA."
Burlington Industries manufactures textile products for apparel and interior furnishings.
